title: Introduction to Python
description: Learn what Python is, its key features, history, and why it is widely used in modern programming and development.

lessons.title: What is Python?
lessons.content: Python is a high-level, interpreted programming language known for its simplicity and readability. It is widely used for web development, data analysis, automation, machine learning, and more.

lessons.title: History and Evolution of Python
lessons.content: Python was created by Guido van Rossum and first released in 1991. It emphasizes code readability and has evolved over time with major versions like Python 2 and Python 3, the latter being the current standard.

lessons.title: Why Choose Python?
lessons.content:
- Easy to learn and read
- Large standard library
- Cross-platform compatibility
- Massive community support
- Ideal for beginners and professionals alike

lessons.title: How Python Works
lessons.content: Python code is interpreted line-by-line at runtime. The interpreter executes the code directly without the need for compilation, which makes development faster and easier.

lessons.title: Python Applications in the Real World
lessons.content:
- Web Development (e.g., Django, Flask)
- Data Science and Machine Learning (e.g., pandas, scikit-learn)
- Automation and Scripting
- Game Development
- Software Testing

lessons.title: Understanding Python Syntax
lessons.content: Python uses indentation instead of braces to define blocks of code. Its syntax is clean and close to natural language, which makes it intuitive for beginners.

lessons.title: Popular Companies Using Python
lessons.content:
- Google
- Instagram
- Netflix
- Dropbox
- NASA
These companies use Python for its reliability, flexibility, and speed of development.

lessons.title: Installing Python: Overview
lessons.content: Python can be installed from the official website (python.org). Most systems come with Python pre-installed. This lesson gives a high-level overview before we dive into setup in the next module.

lessons.title: Python 2 vs Python 3
lessons.content: Python 3 is the present and future of Python. While Python 2 was widely used, it reached end-of-life in 2020. Python 3 offers better syntax, improved features, and active support.

lessons.title: Getting Started with Python Programming
lessons.content: You can write Python using interactive mode (REPL) or in scripts (.py files). Beginners are encouraged to start with small scripts using any text editor or IDE like VS Code.
